title: Work, bureaucracy and formal register
objectives: I can write a formal email or letter with the right greeting, request formulas and closing.
I can handle a job interview and ordinary office situations politely.
I can name the main Brazilian documents and public offices and say what I need from them.
I can choose between o senhor, você and tu depending on the person and the region.
I can pass on a request and refuse politely.

vocabulary.note: Pronounced letter by letter. It is asked for in almost every purchase and registration.

dialogues.title: At the notary office
dialogues.context: Seu Henrique needs a signature notarized and copies certified. The clerk, Sônia, helps him with the formal process.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Bom dia, senhor. O senhor pegou uma senha?
lines.en: Good morning, sir. Did you take a queue number?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Bom dia. Peguei, sim, a de número quarenta e dois.
lines.en: Good morning. Yes, I did, number forty-two.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Pois não, em que posso ajudar o senhor?
lines.en: Of course, how can I help you, sir?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Gostaria de reconhecer firma neste contrato e de autenticar duas cópias do meu RG.
lines.en: I would like to have my signature notarized on this contract and certify two copies of my ID.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Perfeito. O senhor trouxe o documento original e o CPF?
lines.en: Perfect. Did you bring the original document and your CPF?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Trouxe o RG e a CNH. O CPF eu não trouxe, mas o número está na CNH.
lines.en: I brought my ID and my driver's license. I didn't bring my CPF, but the number is on the license.

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Sem problema. Preciso só que o senhor assine aqui na minha frente.
lines.en: No problem. I just need you to sign here in front of me.

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: Claro. Pronto. Quanto fica o total?
lines.en: Of course. Done. How much is the total?

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Fica em quarenta reais. O senhor prefere pagar em dinheiro ou no cartão?
lines.en: It comes to forty reais. Would you prefer to pay in cash or by card?

lines.speaker: Henrique
lines.pt: No cartão, por favor. Até que horas vai o expediente?
lines.en: By card, please. Until what time are you open?

lines.speaker: Sônia
lines.pt: Até as dezessete horas, caso o senhor precise voltar. Aqui está o recibo.
lines.en: Until five p.m., in case you need to come back. Here is your receipt.

dialogues.title: A job interview
dialogues.context: Gabriel is interviewing for a position at an office. The interviewer, Patrícia, is a manager. Note that she calls him você, while he addresses her as a senhora.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Bom dia, Gabriel. Fique à vontade. Obrigada por ter vindo.
lines.en: Good morning, Gabriel. Make yourself comfortable. Thank you for coming.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Bom dia, doutora. Obrigado pela oportunidade.
lines.en: Good morning, doctor. Thank you for the opportunity.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Li o seu currículo. Você pode me falar um pouco sobre a sua experiência?
lines.en: I read your CV. Can you tell me a little about your experience?

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Claro. Trabalhei quatro anos numa loja de eletrônicos, no atendimento ao cliente. Depois fui promovido a supervisor.
lines.en: Of course. I worked four years at an electronics store, in customer service. Then I was promoted to supervisor.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: E por que você saiu de lá?
lines.en: And why did you leave?

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Eu queria uma oportunidade com mais chance de crescimento. A senhora poderia me explicar como funciona o plano de carreira aqui?
lines.en: I wanted an opportunity with more room for growth. Could you explain how the career plan works here?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Claro. Depois de seis meses, há uma avaliação de desempenho, e as promoções são discutidas uma vez por ano.
lines.en: Of course. After six months there is a performance review, and promotions are discussed once a year.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: A vaga é de carteira assinada? E qual é o horário de trabalho?
lines.en: Is the position formal employment? And what are the working hours?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: É de carteira assinada, das nove às dezoito horas, de segunda a sexta. O salário e os benefícios serão detalhados na proposta.
lines.en: It is formal employment, from nine to six, Monday to Friday. The salary and benefits will be detailed in the offer.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Perfeito. Quando a senhora pretende dar uma resposta?
lines.en: Perfect. When do you plan to give an answer?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Entraremos em contato por e-mail até sexta-feira. Infelizmente, hoje não posso adiantar mais nada.
lines.en: We will contact you by email by Friday. Unfortunately, I can't say anything more today.

lines.speaker: Gabriel
lines.pt: Combinado. Muito obrigado, doutora, e uma ótima tarde.
lines.en: Agreed. Thank you very much, doctor, and have a great afternoon.

dialogues.title: Opening an account at the bank
dialogues.context: Dona Marta goes with her daughter Letícia to the bank to open a checking account. The manager, Rodrigo, explains what is missing.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Boa tarde, dona Marta. Em que posso ajudar a senhora?
lines.en: Good afternoon, Dona Marta. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Boa tarde, Rodrigo. Minha filha quer abrir uma conta corrente, e eu vim acompanhar.
lines.en: Good afternoon, Rodrigo. My daughter wants to open a checking account, and I came along.

lines.speaker: Letícia
lines.pt: Boa tarde. Eu trouxe o RG, o CPF e o comprovante de residência.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I brought my ID, my CPF and my proof of address.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Ótimo, deixa eu conferir. O comprovante precisa estar no seu nome e ser dos últimos três meses.
lines.en: Great, let me check. The proof of address must be in your name and from the last three months.

lines.speaker: Letícia
lines.pt: Ele está no nome da minha mãe, porque eu moro com ela.
lines.en: It is in my mother's name, because I live with her.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Entendi. Infelizmente não posso aceitar assim, mas tem uma solução. A dona Marta pode assinar uma declaração dizendo que a senhora mora com ela.
lines.en: I see. Unfortunately I can't accept it like that, but there is a solution. Dona Marta can sign a declaration saying that you live with her.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Posso assinar agora mesmo. Preciso reconhecer firma no cartório?
lines.en: I can sign right now. Do I need to have my signature notarized at the notary office?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Não precisa, a senhora assina aqui na minha frente. Depois disso eu agendo a entrega do cartão.
lines.en: No need, you sign here in front of me. After that I will schedule the delivery of the card.

lines.speaker: Letícia
lines.pt: Que alívio! E tem alguma tarifa mensal?
lines.en: What a relief! And is there a monthly fee?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Para esta conta, não tem. O cartão chega na sua casa em até sete dias úteis.
lines.en: For this account, there isn't. The card arrives at your home within seven business days.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Muito obrigada, meu filho. Foi um ótimo atendimento.
lines.en: Thank you very much, dear. It was excellent service.

grammar.title: Formal register: o senhor, a senhora and written conventions
grammar.explanation:
Formal Portuguese is built on third person verb forms and titles. To be respectful to an older person, a stranger in a service situation, a client or a superior, use o senhor or a senhora with the third person singular verb: O senhor quer um café? A senhora trouxe o RG? Você is the neutral everyday form, and o senhor adds respect and distance. Brazilians also use titles with first names: dona Marta, seu Henrique, doutora Patrícia (doutor and doutora are used for doctors, lawyers and other professionals, not only for people with doctorates).

In writing, formal emails and letters follow a fixed frame. The opening is Prezado senhor, Prezada senhora, Prezados senhores or Prezado Paulo Andrade, followed by a comma. The closing is Atenciosamente or Cordialmente, then the name. Cordialmente is a little warmer, and Att. is the common abbreviation in short messages. In informal workplace emails Olá, João is also acceptable, but it is wise to start formal with someone you do not know.

When in doubt, err on the side of respect with older people and in public offices. Conversations with colleagues usually become more relaxed quickly, and você is then the normal choice.

examples.en: Could you wait a moment, sir?

grammar.title: Request formulas for polite requests
grammar.explanation:
Formal requests rely on the conditional and on fixed phrases. Gostaria de plus an infinitive (Gostaria de solicitar, Gostaria de saber) is softer than Eu quero. Poderia plus an infinitive (Poderia me informar...?, Poderia repetir, por favor?) is a polite question. In writing, Venho por meio desta (literally, I come by means of this) announces the purpose of the message and is used mostly at the start of a formal letter: Venho por meio desta solicitar a segunda via do documento.

Other useful phrases: Solicito (I request), Gostaria de agendar, Segue em anexo (attached is), Fico à disposição (I am at your disposal), Aguardo retorno (I await your reply), Agradeço desde já (thanks in advance), Conforme conversamos (as we discussed). The pronoun me usually comes before the verb in Brazilian usage: Poderia me informar, not Poderia informar-me.

In speech, people soften further with por favor, com licença and por gentileza. A request without any of these can sound abrupt in a public office, even if grammatically correct.

grammar.title: Tu, você and o senhor: choosing address forms
grammar.explanation:
Brazilian Portuguese has three main ways of saying you to one person. Você is the standard everyday form across most of Brazil, used with the third person singular verb. O senhor and a senhora are formal. Tu is used in parts of the country, especially the far south (Rio Grande do Sul), parts of the north and northeast, and in some neighborhoods of Rio de Janeiro, but the verb that goes with it varies a lot.

In the south, speakers often use tu with the correct tu verb forms: Tu falas, tu queres. In many other regions tu is used with the third person verb: Tu fala, tu quer. Both are common in speech, but written formal Portuguese expects você, o senhor or the correct tu forms. As a learner, you can use você everywhere and understand tu when you hear it. Do not use tu in formal situations.

Imperatives follow the same split: formal Sente-se, Aguarde, Entre (from the você and o senhor forms) versus the casual Senta aí, Espera, Entra that you will hear in the south or among close friends. In a request to a stranger in an office, always prefer the formal imperative or, better, a polite question: O senhor poderia aguardar?

grammar.title: Reported requests and polite refusals
grammar.explanation:
At work you often have to pass on what someone asked you to do. The simplest pattern is pedir para plus subject plus infinitive: Ela pediu para eu enviar o contrato; or pedir que plus the subjunctive: Ela pediu que eu enviasse o contrato (imperfect subjunctive, because the request is in the past). In speech the first is much more common: Pediram pra você assinar. For orders and instructions, mandar is stronger: O chefe mandou entregar hoje. To report what was said: Ele disse que ia ligar, Ela falou que o prazo terminou.

Polite refusals avoid a direct não. Typical formulas are Infelizmente não será possível, Lamento informar que..., No momento não temos vagas, Agradeço o convite, mas não poderei comparecer, Receio que não seja possível. Add a reason or an alternative: Infelizmente não será possível hoje, mas podemos agendar para segunda.

Compare the direct versions that would be rude in a formal setting: Não, não dá, or Isso não pode. In a friendly conversation Não dá, desculpa is perfectly fine, but at a counter or in a letter the longer formula is expected.

Agradeço o convite, mas não poderei comparecer.

culture.title: A burocracia brasileira
culture.text:
Brazilian bureaucracy has a reputation for papers, stamps and queues, and a few words tell the story. The cartório is an office, run privately under public authority, where you register births and marriages, notarize signatures (reconhecer firma) and certify copies (autenticar). The CPF number is asked for at pharmacies, shops and websites, and cashiers often ask Quer CPF na nota? Many people hire a despachante, a professional who handles paperwork for them, especially for cars and property.

Working life has its own vocabulary. A job with carteira assinada means formal employment with legal protections: paid vacation, a thirteenth-month salary (décimo terceiro) paid in December, and a contribution to a savings fund called FGTS. In recent years many services have moved online, through the government portal gov.br, and the work booklet is now digital, but physical queues, with a numbered ticket (a senha), remain common at the INSS, the bank and city hall.

Income tax is declared to the Receita Federal every year, with a deadline in spring that makes the news. In offices, the tone is polite and the title is important: Seu José, dona Rita, doutora Ana. A smile and a por favor go a long way at the counter, and so does patience.

paragraphs.pt: Prezada senhora Fernanda Lima, venho por meio desta me candidatar à vaga de analista administrativo, anunciada no site da empresa no dia dez de março.
paragraphs.en: Dear Ms. Fernanda Lima, I am writing to apply for the administrative analyst position, advertised on the company website on March tenth.

paragraphs.pt: Sou formado em Administração e tenho três anos de experiência em atendimento e organização de documentos. Segue em anexo o meu currículo.
paragraphs.en: I have a degree in Business Administration and three years of experience in customer service and document organization. My CV is attached.

paragraphs.pt: Gostaria de saber se é possível agendar uma entrevista na próxima semana. Também gostaria de solicitar informações sobre o salário e os benefícios oferecidos.
paragraphs.en: I would like to know whether it is possible to schedule an interview next week. I would also like to request information about the salary and benefits offered.

paragraphs.pt: Fico à disposição para qualquer esclarecimento. Atenciosamente, Paulo Andrade.
paragraphs.en: I am at your disposal for any clarification. Sincerely, Paulo Andrade.

paragraphs.pt: Prezado senhor Paulo, agradecemos o seu interesse. Infelizmente, não será possível marcar a entrevista na próxima semana, pois a agenda da gerência está completa.
paragraphs.en: Dear Mr. Paulo, thank you for your interest. Unfortunately, it will not be possible to schedule the interview next week, since the management calendar is full.

paragraphs.pt: As informações sobre salário e benefícios serão passadas durante a entrevista. O senhor poderia comparecer à nossa sede no dia vinte e dois, às catorze horas?
paragraphs.en: Information about salary and benefits will be given during the interview. Could you come to our headquarters on the twenty-second, at two p.m.?

paragraphs.pt: Pedimos que traga o RG, o CPF e um comprovante de residência. Cordialmente, Fernanda Lima.
paragraphs.en: We ask that you bring your ID, your CPF and a proof of address. Cordially, Fernanda Lima.
